messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 detected in azd (eu-west-3) - networking degradation: high NAT conntrack usage + route propagation lag. Affected private subnets; PagerDuty PD-7432
maria-oncall: I'm awake and taking lead. Starting investigation. @kevin-neteng are you on network? @jason-support can you pull any customer impact reports?
kevin-neteng: digging in now. NAT gateway metrics show nat-0f1e2d3c at 92% conntrack and nat-0a9b8c7d at weird state. Also seeing duplicate default routes in rtb-0a1b2c3d. Lots of SYN_RECV entries.
jason-support: customers reporting outbound failures ~09:18 UTC, 502s and timeouts to external providers. Tickets: #5234, #5237, #5241.
sophie-sre: paste the route table dump & any recent infra runs pls, I'll check propagation and recent deploys.
kevin-neteng: route table dump:
```
RouteTableId: rtb-0a1b2c3d
Associations:
 - subnet-azd-priv-1
 - subnet-azd-priv-2
Routes:
 - 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0f1e2d3c (state active) (propagated: false)
 - 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0a9b8c7d (state blackhole) (propagated: true)
 - 10.0.0.0/16 -> local
```
kevin-neteng: note the second default route points to a NAT that's in blackhole state but still present and flagged as propagated. Last modify by terraform-runner at 3805004000.
maria-oncall: traceroute from app in subnet-priv-1 to 8.8.8.8 shows drop after NAT:
```
traceroute to 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1) 0.42 ms
 2 * * *
 3 * * *
```
olga-platops: confirmed a terraform apply at 3805003980 touched route_table_assoc for many subnets in az-d. Possible race where assoc/resolution happened before NAT resource fully ready.
kevin-neteng: conntrack overflow explains connection drops; connections flapping between NATs cause external calls to fail.
frank-ntwk: quick mitigation: remove the blackholed 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0a9b8c7d route from rtb-0a1b2c3d and ensure subnets are explicitly associated to the healthy NAT nat-0f1e2d3c. If needed create replacement NAT and shift traffic.
maria-oncall: executing replace-route to point default route at nat-0f1e2d3c and re-associate subnet-azd-priv-1 now. Posting command and output.
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3d --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0f1e2d3c
```
replace-route: OK
kevin-neteng: association confirmed for subnet-azd-priv-1 -> rtb-0a1b2c3d; route table now shows single default route to nat-0f1e2d3c.
sophie-sre: running synthetic checks against payment endpoints from app hosts in az-d:
```
curl -v --max-time 10 https://payments.prod.internal/health
* Connected to 10.200.5.12 (10.200.5.12) port 443
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
sophie-sre: looks healthy from the instance I ran against. Kevin, please monitor NAT conntrack metrics for 10 minutes and report trend.
kevin-neteng: conntrack usage dropping 98% -> 66% over last 3 minutes. SYN_RECV counts decreasing, egress success rising. :thumbsup:
jason-support: ticket #5237 updated by customer: "services resumed ~09:22, thanks". marking as partial recovery.
maria-oncall: Preliminary customer impact: ~12% of customers in az-d experienced outbound failures for ~14 minutes starting ~09:18 UTC. Payment flows and webhooks affected. No data loss or compromise. Severity P1 due to payments impact.
olga-platops: paused the terraform pipeline that touched route associations and opened a PR to add locking & explicit resource ordering for route_table_assoc and NAT creation.
sophie-sre: drafting full incident RCA and action items: 1) add CI guard to prevent route assoc before NAT readiness 2) add alert for duplicate default routes in same RT 3) document conntrack scaling and pre-warm guidance 4) test idempotent route apply in infra tests.
frank-ntwk: adding alert tuning: detect duplicate 0.0.0.0/0 routes pointing to different targets, and rapid changes in route propagation flags.
eve-product: we'll prepare a customer-facing summary + apology and schedule follow-up with affected accounts.
maria-oncall: Handoff: handing to sophie-sre for longer-term remediation & postmortem. I'll remain on-call for escalation for next 25 minutes. Incident will remain P1 until runbook items verified.
incident-bot: Incident PD-7432 state -> monitoring. Assigned to sophie-sre.
sophie-sre: taking over. Opening incident doc and scheduling postmortem. Thanks for fast mitigation everyone. :clap:
jason-support: closing affected customer tickets as resolved with note "service resumed; monitoring".
olga-platops: CI fixes queued; PR will go after review.
sophie-sre: last_message: marking thread closed in Slack; will update PD and postmortem when RCA ready.
